newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen mixed to softer at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen mixed to softer at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open mixed to slightly lower on Thursday, bolstered by bargain hunting after yesterday's weak and volatile session but wary of a soft bond market after a decline in jobless claims.
Initial jobless claims for the week ended June 21 fell by 14,000 to 332,000, against a forecast drop of 7,000 claims.
"The jobless claims decline hit the bond market, and stocks could open a little weaker here," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said.
The long bond was lower, off 9/32 at a 6.76 percent yield.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off 1.95 points at 894.30.

"The (stock) market has been bothered for the past couple of days by the weakness in the bond market, and that should carry through today," Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said.
But Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics, said because jobless claims were a weekly data, they would not necessarily create huge turmoil in stocks.
Technology stocks were also expected to come under pressure after several earnings warnings in that sector.
